verses.1: After the citizens departed, the king, an expert in decisionmaking again consulted his counsellors and said, Tomorrow Pushya star is in the ascendence and my son, Rama (handsome) with coppercoloured eyes which resemble red lotus petals will be installed heirapparent.
verses.2: After the citizens departed, the king, an expert in decisionmaking again consulted his counsellors and said, Tomorrow Pushya star is in the ascendence and my son, Rama (handsome) with coppercoloured eyes which resemble red lotus petals will be installed heirapparent.
verses.3: Therafter king Dasaratha on retiring to his private apartment, ordered Sumantra to bring Rama once again.
verses.4: In obedience to the command of the king charioteer Sumantra set out speedily to the palace of Rama to fetch him back once again.
verses.5: The doorkeepers informed Rama of Sumantra's arrival. As soon as he learnt that Sumantra was back again, Rama was filled with apprehensions.
verses.6: Rama got Sumantra admitted and said to him, What is the purpose of your coming back so quickly ? Tell me whatever is there without holding back.
verses.7: Then Sumantra replied, 'The king desires to see you. To go or not to go, the decision is yours'.
verses.8: On hearing the words of the charioteer, Rama immediately set out for the royal palace to see the king again.
verses.9: Having heard of Rama's arrival, king Dasaratha got him admitted into his apartment to tell him something very pleasant.
verses.10: On entering his father's palace, glorious Rama, folded his hands and bent low in reverence from a distance and beheld his father.
verses.11: As he (Rama) was bending (with reverence), Dasaratha lifted him up and embraced him. Thereafter, he offered him a splendid seat and said again:
verses.12: O Rama after a long life I have grown old. I have enjoyed all the pleasures I desired. I have also performed hundreds of rituals which enjoined distribution of abundant food and gifts.
verses.13: O best of men I have obtained now a progeny of my liking in you and you have no equal on earth. I have given gifts, performed rituals and also studied (the Vedas) .
verses.14: O mighty son I have experienced all the pleasures I longed for. I redeemed my debt to the gods, the sages, my ancestors, brahmins and to myself.
verses.15: There is nothing left to be done by me except your consecration Hence you should perform what I tell you.
verses.16: Today all the subjects expresed their desire to see you as their king. Therefore, my dear son, I wish to coronate you heirapparent.
verses.17: Moreover Rama, these days I see frightening and ominous events in dreams during day time. I see meteors accompanied by thunders falling, generating great sounds.
verses.18: O Rama astrologers also tell me that formidable planets Sun, Mars and Rahu have afflicted my birth star.
verses.19: When such ominous signs appear, usually the king either meets with death or faces a grave calamity.
verses.20: Therefore, before my mind is deluded I wish to see you installed as heirapparent for a man's mind is unstable indeed, O Rama.
verses.21: Today the Moon is in conjunction with the Punarvasu constellation. Tomorrow the Moon's conjunction with the Pushya constellation is certain and the astrologers say this auspicious time is highly suitable for the purpose of coronation.
verses.22: ﻿﻿ My mind is hastening me saying, 'Coronate Rama in the Pushya constellation itself'. O Slayer of enemies, I shall install you heir apparent tomorrow.
verses.23: Therefore, you and my daughterinlaw (Sita) should fast tonight and sleep on a bed of darbha or kusha grass with selfrestraint.
verses.24: Many impediments befall acts of this sort indeed. Alert your friends to protect you from all sides today onwards.
verses.25: While Bharata is away from the city, the time is favourable for your installation. This is my opinion.
verses.26: It is true, your brother Bharata has adhered to the path of the virtuous and has followed his elder brother. No doubt, he is righteous, compassionate and self controlled.
verses.27: Yet I think even the propitious minds of those who are virtuous and whose thoughts are fixed in righteousness can also become fickle.
verses.28: Having spoken to Rama about the installation ceremony fixed for the next day, he (Dasaratha) permitted him to leave saying, 'You may go'. Rama paid obeisance to his father and returned to his abode.
verses.29: With the installation fixed by the king, Rama went into his residence but left immediately to see his mother in her inner apartment.
verses.30: There he beheld his mother in silk apparel engrossed in silent prayer (to the gods) for his royal fortune in the room meant for the worship of the gods.
verses.31: Hearing the welcome tidings of the installation of her beloved Rama, Sita too, had been brought in. Sumitra and Lakshmana had already arrived there.
verses.32: At that moment Kausalya was meditating with her eyes halfclosed. Sumitra, Lakshmana and Sita were attending on her.
verses.33: Having heard that installation of her son as heirapparent was planned in Pushya constellation, Kausalya was meditating upon the Supreme Person, Lord Visnu by controlling her breath (Pranayama).
verses.34: While she (Kausalya) was in that state of meditation, Rama approached her, offered reverential salutation and said these words of praise enhancing her joy:
verses.35: "Whatever rites here are fitting for the consecration that is to take place tomorrow, have those auspicious rites performed today for me and for Vaidehi."
verses.36: Hearing this, which she had longed for through so long a time, Kausalya, choked with tears of joy, spoke these words to Rama.
verses.37: "Live long, dear child Rama. Your adversaries are destroyed. Endowed with royal fortune, gladden my kinsfolk and those of Sumitra."
verses.38: "Surely it was under an auspicious constellation that I bore you, dear son, since by your virtues you have won your father Dasaratha."
verses.39: "Surely my endurance in this lotus-eyed man was not in vain, my son, since this very royal fortune of the Ikshvakus shall now attend upon you."
verses.40: Addressed in this wise by his mother, Rama looked upon his brother, who sat bowing with joined palms, and said to him, smiling as it were:
verses.41: "Lakshmana, rule this earth along with me. This royal fortune has come to you, who are my second self."
verses.42: "Enjoy, Saumitri, the enjoyments you desire and the fruits of the kingdom. It is for your sake that I desire my life and the kingdom too."
verses.43: Having spoken thus to Lakshmana, Rama saluted his mothers, took leave of Sita, and went to his own dwelling.
